findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The supplied Functional check exercises invoke failures, oversized outbound messages and error redaction, but skips the covered user journeys: authenticated inbound text receiving an agent reply, proactive delivery after restart, and an unauthorized approval followed by a permitted decision. The brief explicitly requires the functional check to walk every covered Done-when item. Exercise those journeys and record what happened; a live Teams tenant is not necessary if the real application boundaries are exercised with Microsoft faked at its edge.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body:
chunk 2/3:

The inbound-text end-to-end case explicitly calls `recover()` and later calls `queue.enqueueMessageCheck()` itself. These steps bypass the production recovery and admission-loop wiring that must turn an acknowledged Teams message into an agent reply. The test can therefore pass while that wiring is disconnected. Start the production recovery/admission path in this case and assert that the HTTP submission produces the reply without manually advancing messages through internal services.
findings.title: Not done: automatic Teams ingress recovery end-to-end proof

findings.body:
chunk 2/3:

The supplied Functional check describes invoke failure envelopes, connector 413 splitting, and error redaction, but does not exercise the covered proactive delivery after restart or unauthorized-then-authorized approval flow. The review contract explicitly requires the functional check to walk every covered Done-when item. Exercise those flows and record their observed outcomes; the automated cases' existence alone does not establish that this walkthrough happened.
findings.title: Not done: functional check
